title: 2010 eruptions of Eyjafjallajökull
summary: Iceland's Eyjafjallajökull erupted in 2010, first as a fissure eruption at Fimmvörðuháls from 20 March, then from the ice-covered summit caldera from 14 April. The summit eruption produced fine ash and meltwater floods. Ash drifting over Europe halted most commercial flights for nearly a week, with economic impacts in the billions.

when.display: 20 March – 22 May 2010 (activity ceased by late June 2010)

as_recorded.value: began as a fissure eruption on 20 March 2010

reviewer_note: Sources differ on end: sustained activity ended 22 May, ash last seen in June, and the eruption was declared over in October; I used 2010 for both years. The first source is a Smithsonian page with a long navigation header; the second is a paper abstract and only partly covers the eruption. The Wikidata end date of 27 October reflects the declaration of the eruption's end, not activity.} (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from Smithsonian Institution, agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com; quotes machine-checked.)
